title: Pointers Are Variables That Hold Addresses
summary: A pointer is an ordinary variable whose value is an address. Its type says what kind of value lives at that address. Declaring, initialising and printing pointers, nullptr for "no address", and why int* and double* are different types even though both are 8 bytes.

cards.q: int* p{ &score }; What is the value stored in p, and what is the value of &p?
cards.a: p holds score's address. &p is the address of p itself, a different place in memory.

cards.q: In int* a, b; what type is b?
cards.a: A plain int. The star applies to a only.

cards.q: Why will the compiler not let an int* hold the address of a double?
cards.a: The pointer's type says how to read the bytes at the address. Reading a double's bytes as an int is meaningless, so the conversion needs an explicit cast.
No. They hold equal values but are two different objects at two different addresses.
